coverageNote: Completed 3a implementer simulation, 3b Vision Rubric scoring, and 3c devil's-advocate probing for all 58 scoped Markdown source files across 10 audit units.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records provide Owner and Deferred To but omit both a deadline and the decision blocked; manifest authority is still unresolved.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
Who owns the manifest when a venue hosts an external promoter's show — Operator or the promoter?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the authority that owns manifests, holds, and release notifications for promoter-led shows.
findings.failureScenario: A promoter hold has no authorized actor, so staff either bypass access controls or leave sellable inventory stranded.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records omit a deadline and explicit blocked decision, including who can make an on-sale decision for an external promoter show.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
Who is the on-sale's decision-maker when a venue hosts an external promoter's show?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the actor allowed to schedule, amend, and release an externally promoted on-sale.
findings.failureScenario: An on-sale can be opened, delayed, or changed by the wrong party during a live commercial dispute.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records omit a deadline and explicit blocked decision for comp-budget source-of-truth ownership.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
Do comp budgets originate as deal terms in domain 17 and flow here, or are they re-keyed by the Operator?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether a comp budget is contract-derived or a locally editable ticketing value.
findings.failureScenario: The contract promises 20 comps while the door roster only admits 10, creating a live admission and settlement dispute.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records omit a deadline and explicit blocked decision even though the hardware target determines the offline scanning architecture.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
What is the door hardware target — Operator's own phone, a dedicated scanner, or both?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose device capabilities, operating conditions, and the scan-client deployment target.
findings.failureScenario: A scanner workflow is built against unsupported device capabilities or lacks the offline guarantees required at the door.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records omit a deadline and explicit blocked decision for the promoter or agent recipient that consumes drop reports.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
The Promoter has no persona and is the primary consumer of a drop report.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the counterparty profile, access scope, and delivery authority for promoter and agent reports.
findings.failureScenario: Commercially sensitive sales data is either sent to an unauthorized actor or withheld from the party relying on it.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records omit a deadline and explicit blocked decision for the core refund policy.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
What is the refund policy? Are fees refundable? Are individual refunds granted at all, or only on cancellation?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose refund eligibility, fee treatment, and the individual-refund right.
findings.failureScenario: Two equally situated buyers receive different outcomes because the refund engine has no governing policy.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records omit a deadline and explicit blocked decision for the provider set and legal viability of connectors.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
Which platforms, and in what order? Some have no API or forbid this use in their terms.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose permitted external providers and the connector capabilities that the product will support.
findings.failureScenario: The product ships an integration against a forbidden or unavailable data surface and cannot reconcile externally ticketed shows.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records omit a deadline and explicit blocked decision for the VIP package shape that determines whether merch dependencies are required.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
Whether a ticket-only VIP shape ships first remains open.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether the first VIP offer includes merchandise or only admission and meet-and-greet entitlements.
findings.failureScenario: Implementation begins against merchandise inventory and fulfilment dependencies that the MVP later excludes.

findings.claim: The unit's unresolved-question records omit a deadline and explicit blocked decision for the purchase-limit effect of ticket transfer.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
Does transfer decrement the sender's holding for purchase-limit purposes?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether transferred inventory restores a sender's purchase-limit allowance.
findings.failureScenario: A scalper either bypasses the limit by cycling transfers or a legitimate buyer is permanently locked out after gifting a ticket.

findings.claim: The root open-question record omits a deadline and explicit blocked decision for promoter and agent authority despite their ownership of core ticketing actions.

evidence.excerpt: | # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
The 4-persona model has no PROMOTER, and the promoter and agent are unowned.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the authorization and data-access model for promoter and agent counterparties.
findings.failureScenario: Authority for pricing, on-sale, inventory, and reports is silently assigned to the wrong existing role.

findings.claim: Post-on-sale pricing has no deterministic concurrent-edit rule or price-guarantee policy.

evidence.excerpt: Concurrent edits by Operator staff during a live on-sale are a real race. [PENDING]
A price-level change after on-sale must notify existing buyers only if it lowers the price and a price-guarantee policy exists. [PENDING]
Is a price-guarantee policy platform-wide, per-venue, or per-show?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose update serialization, effective-price precedence, and whether past buyers receive a credit after a decrease.
findings.failureScenario: Two buyers in the same tier are charged different totals or receive inconsistent refunds after a concurrent price change.

findings.claim: Inventory lifecycle precedence and the payment-authorization hold race are intentionally left unresolved.

evidence.excerpt: Hold expiry, window close, and tier advance can all fire on the same inventory within the same second. [PENDING]
Hold expires during payment authorisation ... [PENDING] — a genuine race with money on both sides.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose event ordering, authorization-extension behavior, and compensation when payment succeeds after inventory release.
findings.failureScenario: A buyer is charged for a ticket already returned to inventory, causing oversell or a paid-without-ticket incident.

findings.claim: Access-code partial redemption has no state transition across sessions.

evidence.excerpt: Use count and ticket limit must permit resumption or explicitly not. [PENDING]
Whether a partial redemption leaves a resumable remainder or closes the code is undecided.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the code use-count state machine, remainder expiry, and interaction with the per-buyer limit.
findings.failureScenario: A partially used code either locks allocation indefinitely or is reused to exceed its intended entitlement.

findings.claim: Access-code brute-force protection requires high entropy and throttling but supplies no implementable entropy or rate-limit values.

evidence.excerpt: Codes must be high-entropy and rate-limited ... [PENDING — entropy length + rate-limit thresholds].

findings.forcedInvention: Choose token entropy, per-account and per-IP attempt windows, lock duration, and retry behavior.
findings.failureScenario: Attackers enumerate valid presale codes or legitimate fans are blocked by arbitrary throttling behavior.

findings.claim: Guest-list writes and statement certification have no defined separation-of-duties rule.

evidence.excerpt: The right to add a guest and the right to certify a statement should not sit with the same person unchecked. [PENDING]
A duplicate guest against two party allocations is a real double-admit and settlement question.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the approval, counter-signature, or role-separation rule for door-time guest changes and certification.
findings.failureScenario: One staff member adds uncompensated guests and certifies the resulting count without independent review.

findings.claim: Offline scan conflict ordering, durable peer recovery, and replica PII protection remain uncontracted.

evidence.excerpt: A device that dies with unpushed scans loses them irrecoverably unless peers hold copies.
No mechanism is selected for trusting device clocks enough to order conflicts.
Exactly which PII fields the replica carries and how it is encrypted at rest remain open.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose a durable sync topology, conflict clock, replica field set, encryption boundary, and data lifetime.
findings.failureScenario: A lost or stolen scanner both corrupts the certified attendance count and exposes attendee data.

findings.claim: An ignored stale-manifest warning has no escalation or operational response.

evidence.excerpt: No source in the tree defines any escalation from an ignored amber warning.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose escalation recipients, timing, degraded-mode behavior, and whether new scans can continue.
findings.failureScenario: A scanner stays stale through a whole event, admitting refunded or transferred tickets without an accountable response.

findings.claim: Token re-entry leaves a transferable wristband as an unresolved age-verification credential.

evidence.excerpt: Not re-checking makes the wristband a transferable age credential, which is precisely how a 16-year-old gets in.
Whether an 18+ show needs a distinguishable band is an unresolved risk-acceptance and scope call.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether the system models a physical age band, forces an ID re-check, or accepts the licensing risk.
findings.failureScenario: An under-age person uses a transferred re-entry band to bypass both ticket and ID verification.

findings.claim: Composite age restrictions lack an adult-to-minor binding rule and an authored outcome when a restriction rises after sale.

evidence.excerpt: Whether one adult may vouch for more than one minor is [PENDING].
A restriction raised after tickets sold is treated as a material change and gets a refund route. [PENDING]

findings.forcedInvention: Choose adult-to-minor proof and ratio semantics, and the material-change/refund rule for newly ineligible holders.
findings.failureScenario: Door staff apply inconsistent minor admission rules or deny a paid attendee without a legally and commercially defined remedy.

findings.claim: Cart-expiry inventory at sell-out has contradictory destinations: the waitlist rule and open-storefront behavior both claim the case.

evidence.excerpt: When carted units expire at sell-out, the rules point different ways: route through the waitlist or reappear openly on the storefront.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the routing rule for newly available cart-expiry inventory and its anti-bot behavior.
findings.failureScenario: Some expiring carts create an unannounced public mini-on-sale while waitlisted fans are bypassed.

findings.claim: Sales-pacing alerts lack the measurable reference curve, cold-start model, and numeric alert bands that determine when an Operator is warned.

evidence.excerpt: The specific curve shape, per-genre and per-room fitting, and cold-start default are [PENDING].
Exact percentages and alert bands are [PENDING].

findings.forcedInvention: Choose a baseline curve, data source, cold-start behavior, alert percentages, and alert-band semantics.
findings.failureScenario: A healthy show is incorrectly escalated or a genuinely failing on-sale receives no actionable warning.

findings.claim: The settlement consequence of a lapsed or declined counter-attestation is unresolved.

evidence.excerpt: May settlement run on a single-party-certified, un-countered statement, or is a counter-attestation a hard precondition for payout?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether a lapse blocks payout, permits payout with disclosure, or triggers another resolution path.
findings.failureScenario: Settlement either pays on an unagreed count or indefinitely strands funds when a counterparty is unresponsive.

findings.claim: Refund eligibility and reschedule or postponement windows are still owner choices without authored policy values.

evidence.excerpt: What is the refund policy? Are fees refundable? Are individual refunds granted at all, or only on cancellation?
How long is the opt-out window, and what sets it — statute, deal, or platform policy?
What is the postponement deadline — a fixed platform period, or jurisdiction-derived?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose refund eligibility, fee handling, opt-out duration, and the date at which postponement turns into a remedy.
findings.failureScenario: Buyers receive inconsistent refund outcomes and inventory remains frozen indefinitely after a postponed show.

findings.claim: Mass refunds lack an approved alternative payout rail for dead payment methods and an unclaimed-cash disposition rule.

evidence.excerpt: Which alternative rail is offered when the original payment method is dead — store credit, bank transfer, or manual payout?
What unclaimed-funds retention and legally permitted handoff procedure applies to an unpresented anonymous cash-refund claim?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose fallback payment rails, identity checks, retention periods, and legally permitted disposition of unclaimed funds.
findings.failureScenario: Cancelled-event refunds become unrecoverable liabilities or are routed through an unauthorized payout and retention process.

findings.claim: Cross-currency external sales preserve source currency but do not define the FX rate source, timing, or rounding used for settlement.

evidence.excerpt: Conversion is a settlement-time act with an explicit, timestamped rate; FX mechanics are [PENDING].
Rate source, timing, rounding, and settlement mechanics remain open.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the rate provider, rate timestamp, rounding boundaries, failure handling, and audit record.
findings.failureScenario: The two sides settle the same foreign-currency sale using different exchange rates and disagree on payout.

findings.claim: VIP package component remedies and transfer semantics are unresolved even though the components have different recipients and fulfillment states.

evidence.excerpt: A fan who misses a meet-and-greet slot has a non-retryable fulfilment and what is owed is [PENDING].
Whether a transferred package's meet-and-greet is honored by default or requires artist consent is unresolved.
Cancelled show with shipped goods: the physical-goods refund treatment remains open.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose component-level remedies, artist-consent requirements, merchandise ownership, and transfer effects on the meet-and-greet roster.
findings.failureScenario: A buyer receives a refund, a stranger appears on the artist roster, or shipped merchandise is charged twice after cancellation.

findings.claim: Purchase limits depend on an undefined buyer-assurance model and unresolved transfer-accounting rule.

evidence.excerpt: Concurrent purchases across accounts racing one limit are [PENDING].
The assurance level of a buyer's account at checkout is a question that no ideation file owns.
Whether transfer decrements the sender's holding is a rule in the transfer and limit-check contracts.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose account assurance, cross-account correlation, concurrent-limit serialization, and whether transferred tickets restore allowance.
findings.failureScenario: A scalper uses low-assurance accounts and transfers to defeat the cap, or a legitimate fan is unfairly blocked.

findings.claim: The resale exchange lacks its required money-to-ticket commit and compensating-reversal contract.

evidence.excerpt: The charge does not stand unless the holder change commits; the commit-and-compensating-reversal mechanism is [PENDING].

findings.forcedInvention: Choose transaction boundaries, idempotency keys, reversal timing, ownership-lock semantics, and recovery after partial failure.
findings.failureScenario: A buyer is charged without receiving the ticket, or a seller is paid while still retaining a usable admission token.

findings.claim: Resale does not define face value after fees or priority between a fan listing and unsold venue inventory.

evidence.excerpt: What is face value once fees exist? Whether a reseller is made whole on fees remains an owner policy.
When a fan lists while the venue has unsold inventory, who sells first is unresolved.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the fee-inclusive resale cap, buyer and seller fee treatment, and inventory-ordering rule.
findings.failureScenario: The exchange either violates its advertised price cap or unfairly suppresses a fan listing to protect venue sales.

findings.claim: Attendee-data consent scope and withdrawal after export are unresolved at the boundary where legal duties must be enforced.

evidence.excerpt: Is consent per-event, per-artist, or per-venue?
How does withdrawal propagate once a party has exported the list off-platform?
Propagation past the platform boundary is a duty the platform can signal but not enforce. [PENDING]

findings.forcedInvention: Choose consent scope, retention and renewal rules, export terms, revocation notices, and third-party accountability.
findings.failureScenario: A party continues marketing after consent withdrawal or the same person is subjected to inconsistent consent prompts.

findings.claim: RSVP admission is not bounded for an unregistered private room and has no policy when a free event becomes ticketed.

evidence.excerpt: An unregistered private room is the residual open case and the feature can operate outside a venue.
Whether existing RSVPs are honored free, converted, prioritized, or voided when the show becomes ticketed is [PENDING].

findings.forcedInvention: Choose capacity and safety authority outside a registered venue, plus the commercial conversion rule for existing RSVPs.
findings.failureScenario: An unlicensed or over-capacity private event is admitted without a governing cap, or RSVP holders are charged or refused inconsistently.

findings.claim: Promoter and agent authority is not represented by a role even though those actors own on-sale, pricing, and report consumption in real ticketing workflows.

evidence.excerpt: The promoter buys the show, sets the price and owns the on-sale, but the promoter and agent are unowned.
The Promoter has no persona and is the primary consumer of a drop report.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether these actors become counterparty profiles and their permitted inventory, pricing, and report actions.
findings.failureScenario: Existing Operator or Musician accounts are overloaded with promoter powers, exposing price and sales data to the wrong party.

findings.claim: The external-ticketing door-scanning decision is unresolved even though reconciliation depends on the independent scanned count.

evidence.excerpt: Does WeJammin scan tickets on externally-ticketed shows? The door and reconciliation stand or fall together.
If the incumbent owns the barcode, the door is theirs and reconciliation loses its independent check.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether external tickets are scannable, how barcode authority is integrated, and the reconciliation level when they are not.
findings.failureScenario: The system claims independently reconciled external attendance while only re-reporting the venue's own numbers.
